The Hutts are gangsters...|[[Quarsh Panaka]]|{{Film|I}}}} '''Hutts''' were a large [[Slug (creature)|slug]]-like [[Sentience|sentient]] [[species]] who were [[Homeworld|native]] to the [[planet]] [[Varl]], but considered their homeworld to be [[Nal Hutta]] after abandoning Varl due to the [[Kayfoundo Kapa]]. They were well known as [[Galaxy|galactic]] [[gangster]]s who controlled the [[Hutt Clan]] crime syndicate. One famous Hutt was the [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba]], who ruled a massive [[Jabba's criminal empire|criminal empire]] from his [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]] on [[Tatooine]]. ==Biology and appearance== {{Quote|Never tickle a Hutt.|C-3PO|[[Star Wars (2020) 13|''Star Wars'' (2020) 13]]}} [[File:MyargaElectrocuted-2021THR10.jpg|thumb|left|180px|The skeleton of a Hutt]] Hutts were a massive [[Slug (creature)|slug]]-like [[Reptile|reptiloid]] [[species]] who had large [[mouth]]s and stubby [[Limb|arms]]. They had three [[lung]]s. They were tough and muscular with thick''[[Ultimate Factivity Collection: Star Wars]]'' leathery skin,''[[Lords of the Sith]]'' which was wrinkled and slimy. Hutts often had watery [[eye]]s and slack facial expressions. Their tails were supported by a skeletal spine and allowed Hutts to propel themselves through muck which legs would sink into. Despite their legendary adult size, Hutts started out as tiny Huttlets less than half a [[meter]] in height. Hutts possessed skeletons,[[The High Republic (2021) 10|''The High Republic'' (2021) 10]] and were not known for being healthy.''[[Star Wars: Droidography]]'' Some Hutts suffered from a genetic defect that caused their skin to be bereft of pigment and prone to cracking. Whilst the Hutts were originally native to [[Varl]],[[Star Wars Jedi Master Magazine 1|''Star Wars Jedi Master'' Magazine 1]] [[Nal Hutta]]—a planet with a hot [[atmosphere]] that was frequently streaked by greasy rains, creating a fetid sauna in which Hutts were most comfortable—later became the planet that was considered their [[homeworld]]. Hutts were immune to [[mind trick]]s.''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'' [[File:MamatheHutt-HFZ.png|thumb|right|180px|[[Mama]], a Hutt with an enormous size.]] Hutts could live for [[Standard century|centuries]]—Jabba was 604 when he was killed—and could grow to enormous sizes.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' In fact, Hutts' lifespans could span over 1,000 years.''[[Star Wars: Women of the Galaxy]]'' The literary collective term for Hutts was a bulge of Hutts.''[[The High Republic: The Fallen Star]]'' Hutts spent the first 50 [[Standard year|years]] of their life in the [[brood pouch]]es of their [[parent]]s. When they emerged, they were described as having the mind of an infant.{{SW|url=news/the-clone-wars-rewatch-theatrical-release-3-of-3|text=''The Clone Wars'' Rewatch: A Sith Plot Unravels in the Theatrical Release (Part 3 of 3)}} ==History== ===Organized crime=== {{Quote|Rejoice, wretched creatures. Your planet is now the property of the glorious Hutt Cartel.|translated=1|Myarga Anjiliac Atirue|[[The High Republic (2021) 4|''The High Republic'' (2021) 4]]}} The Hutts originally hailed from the planet Varl, where they were hunted by the [[Kayfoundo Kapa]]. In order to escape the Kayfoundo Kapa, the Hutts ultimately abandoned Varl''[[Padawan's Pride]]'' and settled on the planet Nal Hutta. For centuries, the Hutts dominated much of the organized criminal activities in [[the galaxy]]. They dominated the [[Twi'lek]]s of [[Ryloth]] and the [[Nikto]] species for several centuries.[[Bloodline (novel)|''Bloodline'']] The Hutts approached [[Lord]] [[Isamer]] of the [[Directorate]], striking a deal with him to destabilize the local governments of [[Eiram]] and [[E'ronoh]] to the advantage of their long-term plans for control of trade and mass enslavement. To that end, Isamer instigated the [[Eiram–E'ronoh crisis]], but in actuality the Hutts intended for the crisis to destroy the Directorate, allowing them to freely move their criminal operations into the region.''[[The High Republic: Into the Dark]]'' [[File:EnterTheHutts-2021THR4.png|thumb|left|250px|Myarga Anjiliac Atirue leads the Hutt Cartel to Sedri Minor]] During the [[Supreme Chancellor|chancellorship]] of [[Lina Soh]], the Hutts remained quiet''[[The High Republic: Light of the Jedi]]'' and were not known to venture into Republic space due to sanctions upon the Hutt Clans concerning open trade in Republic territory. However, in the wake of the [[Great Hyperspace Disaster]], a Hutt and their guards acquired a ''[[vratixia renanicus]]'' shipment from the [[Sedri system]], and was passing through the [[Kazlin system]] when their [[starship]] was attacked by the [[Nihil]], who killed the Hutt. The wreckage was investigated by [[Sskeer]], [[Keeve Trennis]], and the [[Kotabi]] [[bond-twins]] [[Ceret]] and [[Terec]], and the Hutt's corpse was recovered to [[Starlight Beacon]] by the ''[[Ataraxia]]''.[[The High Republic (2021) 2|''The High Republic'' (2021) 2]] [[Avar Kriss]] requested an autopsy,[[The High Republic (2021) 3|''The High Republic'' (2021) 3]] conducted by [[OrbaLin]] who discovered the cadaver was infected. The infestation was revealed to be [[Drengir]], which burst from the corpse and attacked the [[Jedi]]. Meanwhile, the Hutt Cartel arrived on [[Sedri Minor]] to uphold a bargain struck with the colonists for protection in exchange for regular grain payments. [[Myarga Anjiliac Atirue]] discussed the arrangement with Kriss but was attacked by Sskeer, igniting a battle between the Cartel's [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] and the Jedi until Kriss convinced Myarga to turn her attention to their common enemy, the Drengir, by broadcasting distress calls from across the [[Galactic Frontier]] and [[Nal Hutta]] itself. Though Myarga believed the Five Families would never condone an alliance with the Jedi, she directed her warriors to fight alongside them to battle the Drengir. Trennis was able to convince the Drengir to retreat by performing a [[Mind trick|mind touch]] on Sskeer, communicating the idea that the "meat" on Sedri Minor was spoiled.[[The High Republic (2021) 5|''The High Republic'' (2021) 5]] The uneasy alliance continued in the following months as Avar and Myarga slowed the Drengir infestations across the Frontier.[[The High Republic (2021) 6|''The High Republic'' (2021) 6]] The alliance ended with the defeat of the Drengir during the [[Battle on Mulita|assault on Mulita]]; while Myarga wanted her forces to execute the captured [[Great Progenitor]] of the Drengir, the Jedi defended her as a living being whom they had captured, shattering the alliance.[[The High Republic (2021) 8|''The High Republic'' (2021) 8]] The focus on the Drengir crisis had, however, given the [[Nihil]] marauders time to gather and launch the devastating [[Valo Atrocity]].''[[The High Republic: The Rising Storm]]'' ===A galactic war=== {{Main|Clone Wars}} {{Quote|Perhaps now you will allow the Republic to use your trade routes, and hostilities can come to an end.''"
"''Jabba agrees. A treaty is in order.|Padmé Amidala closes negotiations with Jabba the Hutt through TC-70|audio=HuttTreaty-TCWf.flac|[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]}} [[File:Ziro_before_council_SaV.png|thumb|right|250px|Ziro the Hutt brought before the Grand Hutt Council.]] During the [[Clone Wars]], the [[Galactic Republic]] forged a tacit alliance with the [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] after the [[Jedi]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] and his [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] rescued his son [[Rotta]]. The Republic [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] also foiled a plot by Jabba's uncle [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure|Ziro]] to overthrow his nephew with the collusion of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Later in the war, the renegade [[Sith Lord]] [[Maul]] approached the [[Grand Hutt Council]] on the planet [[Nal Hutta]] to offer them a place in his [[Shadow Collective]]. After denying him, a force of [[bounty hunter]]s attacked Shadow Collective's forces, but after being defeated, saw one of their members, [[Oruba]], killed by [[Savage Opress]]. Eventually, Maul's forces would visit Jabba and [[Gorga Desilijic Aarrpo|Gorga]] on Tatooine and, after a short battle, convinced the two Hutts to join them.{{TCW|Eminence (episode)}} ===Age of the Empire=== {{Quote|For years, the Hutts have enjoyed a special relationship with the Empire. They enjoy protected status in their sector in exchange for performing valuable services for the Empire—outside the bounds of Imperial law. This deal has been in place for decades.|Qi'ra|[[Crimson Reign 1|''Crimson Reign'' 1]]}} During the [[Imperial Era|Age of the Empire]], the Hutts and other organized criminal groups exercised a powerful grip on the galaxy. The Hutts also had extensive dealings with the [[Galactic Empire]][[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']] in return for the protection of Hutt Space. They performed certain important, but off-the-books, services, including helping to run several black-site prisons. When an [[Auction for Han Solo|auction]] intended to sell notorious smuggler and Rebel Alliance member [[Han Solo]], who had been frozen in carbonite and stolen from the [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]], on [[Jekara]] was announced by [[Crimson Dawn]] leader [[Qi'ra]], the Grand Hutt Council, along with the Empire and numerous other criminal factions from across of the galaxy, arrived to join in on the auction. Solo was eventually bought by Jabba, but before Jabba could take his prize, the auction was invaded by [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], who after defeating Qi'ra, ordered his forces to take Solo away as he left to face the rebel [[Luke Skywalker]]. Shortly thereafter, a [[Attack on the Executor|battle in Jekara's orbit]] between the forces of the Hutts and the Imperial forces, provoked by [[Bokku]], began. During the battle, the Grand Hutt Council was killed by Darth Vader, who withdrew from his confrontation with Skywalker after being informed that the [[Darth Sidious|Emperor]] had ordered him to end the Hutt insurrection personally. Jabba was left as the sole leader of the Hutt Clan after Vader's actions, with the Sith Lord also learning that Bokku had been an agent of Crimson Dawn. After Fett reclaimed Solo during the battle, Jabba told Fett of his new position before paying the bounty hunter for delivering Solo to his custody at long last. Jabba ruled until his death during the [[Rescue of Han Solo]]. ===New Republic Era=== {{Quote|The Hutts are in disarray.|[[Rynscar]]|''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''}} Following Jabba's [[Rescue of Han Solo|death]], the Hutts were left to determine who would fill Jabba's seat as leader of his [[Jabba's criminal empire|empire]]. Several months after Jabba's demise, a decision had yet to be made. Following the [[Rebellion on Akiva|liberation]] of [[Akiva]], the [[New Republic]] took steps to curtail the influence of the Hutts and other organized groups by introducing financial regulations and undertaking comprehensive patrols of the galactic shipping lanes. Still, the Hutts were able to exercise some influence over the Nikto species and their government into the New Republic [[New Republic Era|era]]. The Hutts had lost much of their former power over the galactic underworld. As noted by [[Yendor Brethen|Yendor]], other factions, such as [[Rinnrivin Di]]'s [[Rinnrivin Di's cartel|cartel]], were supplanting them and rushing in to gain power in their absence. The Hutts were disliked by both the [[Populists]] and the [[Centrists]], the two main factions in the [[New Republic Senate]]. Several Nikto like Rinnrivin admired [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] for her role in killing Jabba and christened her "Huttslayer." ==Hutts in the galaxy== One [[Unidentified Hutt (Has Obitt)|Hutt]] was based out of [[Sy Myrthian space]] during the Clone Wars. The Hutt hired the smuggler [[Has Obitt]]''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]'' in [[19 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' establishes that the [[Clone Wars]] [[Mission to Mustafar|ended]] in [[19 BBY]]. As ''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]'' establishes that [[Has Obitt]] was working for a [[Unidentified Hutt (Has Obitt)|Hutt]] in [[Sy Myrthian space]] at the same [[time]] as the war's end, he must have been working for the Hutt in 19 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. for a menial job. At some point, the Hutts established but ultimately abandoned settlements on the planet [[Mataou]], where they left behind [[Mataou Hutt security droid|security droids]].''[[Star Wars: Uprising]]'' ==Culture== {{Main|Kajidic}} [[File:Rotta-SWCT.png|thumb|250px|Rotta, a huttlet of the Desilijic kajidic and son of Jabba.]] Hutt society was divided into families known as [[kajidic]]s, Jabba's family was the [[Desilijic]] kajidic, whose mark was [[tattoo]]ed on his arm. Hutts bandaged and buried their dead. [[Classical architectural Hutt style]] could be seen on the planet [[Mataou]]. It was characterized by terraced buildings with sloping gates, and white and red colors.{{WebCite|url=https://playstarwarsuprising.com/game-guide/introduction/#locations|text=Locations|work=Star Wars: Uprising Official Website|archivedate=20160624013822}} Clothing was optional for Hutts, and some would use live [[Sha'rellian toop]]s as hairpieces. Hutts liked to eat [[gorg]]s, [[slime pod]]s, and [[Klatooine paddy frog]]s, and were also known to smoke [[hookah pipe]]s. The Hutts believed that at least one of their own, [[Boonta Hestilic Shad'ruu]], had ascended to [[Deity|godhood]], and held the [[Boonta Eve]] holiday in their honor. Several Hutts known for being crime lords who lived opulent lives overseeing criminal underworld activities like [[spice]] [[Smuggler|smuggling]], [[slavery]], [[gambling]], and [[Bounty hunter|bounty hunting]] in [[Hutt Space]]. They were typically obese, with the muscular [[Nar Shaddaa]] kingpin [[Grakkus Jahibakti Tingi|Grakkus]] being an exception.[[Star Wars (2015) 9|''Star Wars'' (2015) 9]] Not all of this species shared the same interests, however: some Hutts valued art, such as one who, according to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], liked to collect fine porcelain. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:EarlyJabba-ROJSketchbook.png|thumb|left|200px|An early drawing of Jabba]] Hutts first appeared in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], the final installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]]. Early concept art for Jabba the Hutt, and therefore for the Hutt species, by [[Ralph McQuarrie]] depicted Jabba as a fat individual with an immense double chin. Though this design wasn't used in the finished film, it would later inspire the look of [[Azmorigan]], and therefore the [[Jablogian]] species, in ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''.{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/idiots-array-trivia-gallery|text="Idiot's Array" Trivia Gallery}} Coincidentally, the same concept art inspired [[Dyslogia Twang|another species]] in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] lore.{{HoloNetNewsWeb|53|life/13425_1.html|SPECIAL FEATURE: Sightings by Twang}} [[Lucasfilm Story Group]]'s [[Pablo Hidalgo]] stated at [[Celebration Anaheim (2015)|Celebration Anaheim]] that Hutts in [[canon]], unlike in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, each had a single sex.{{SW|url=news/swca-one-big-story-star-wars-canon-panel-liveblog|text=SWCA: One Big Story – ''Star Wars'' Canon Panel Liveblog|nolive=1}} ===Translations=== In many languages, the phrase "[Name] the Hutt" is, or at least used to be before "Hutt" was established as the name of a species, translated as "[Name] ''of'' Hutt." For example, in early Italian-language translations, Jabba's name was sometimes written as "Jabba de' Hutt" (pronounced like the English equivalent, but roughly translating to "Jabba O'Hutt").
